title: Montana Sales Tax: What Businesses Need to Know
summary: Montana has no general sales tax — here's what that means for SaaS businesses, what other taxes apply, and what to know if you sell into other states.
body_text: Montana Sales Tax Quick Facts Montana sales tax rate N/A (no sales tax) Economic nexus threshold N/A (no sales tax) Tax authority Montana Department of Revenue SaaS taxable? No (no sales tax) Administration difficulty N/A ‍ Montana has no sales tax. That means that SaaS , digital products, tangible goods, and services are all tax free in the state. For finance teams, that makes Montana the simplest sales tax jurisdiction in the country. There is nothing to register for, nothing to collect, and no sales tax return to file. This guide covers what no sales tax means in practice, the handful of narrow taxes that do still apply, and the tax obligations Montana-based sellers face when they sell into other states. Montana Sales Tax at a Glance Montana's general sales tax rate is 0%. There is no state rate, no county rate, and no city rate on general retail sales. Unlike states such as Colorado or Texas , where local jurisdictions pile their own rates on top of the state rate, Montana has no state and local tax stack to calculate at all. Montana belongs to the "NOMAD" group of states with no statewide sales tax: New Hampshire, Oregon, Montana, Alaska, and Delaware. (Alaska is the outlier here. It has no state sales tax, but many Alaska localities levy their own local option sales taxes. Montana keeps things simpler.) Why Montana Has No Sales Tax Montana has no sales tax because it funds public services through income, property and excise taxes instead of consumption taxes. Though sales tax has repeatedly come up on Montana ballots, so far citizens have voted every proposal down. Because sales tax is so politically unpopular in the state, it’s unlikely their tax free status will change anytime soon. Excise taxes fill part of the gap. Montana taxes gasoline at 33.75 cents per gallon and cigarettes at $1.70 per pack of 20, and it taxes alcohol and marijuana as well. These excise taxes are built into the transaction, so consumers never see them itemized at checkout the way they would see a sales tax. Taxable Categories: What Montana Does Tax No General Sales Tax Montana taxes nothing under a general sales tax, because it does not have one. Tangible personal property, SaaS, digital goods, groceries, clothing, and services are all untaxed at the point of sale. Businesses selling into or within Montana do not need a sales tax permit, do not collect sales tax from Montana customers, and have no sales and use tax remittance obligations to the state. Transaction-Specific Taxes That Still Apply Montana does levy a short list of targeted taxes on specific transactions, mostly aimed at tourism and regulated products. If your business operates in one of these categories, you have collection obligations even in a no-sales-tax state. Tax Type Rate Where it Applies Local resort tax 3–4% Qualifying resort communities such as Whitefish, Big Sky, West Yellowstone, and Red Lodge Lodging tax 8% combined Hotels, short-term rentals, campgrounds, other accommodations Rental car tax 4% All rental vehicles Medical marijuana tax 4% Dispensary purchases Recreational marijuana tax 20% Dispensary purchases; localities can add up to 3% Gasoline excise tax 33.75 cents per gallon Fuel sales, built into price at pump Cigarette excise tax $1.70 per pack Tobacco sales, built into retail price ‍ It’s important to note that businesses subject to the resort tax must register and file/pay with the locality in which the resort is located. Monitoring: Out-of-State Sales Tax Obligations for Montana Sellers Montana businesses owe no sales tax on sales delivered within Montana. But if you sell online, selling from Montana into other states can create sales tax nexus in those states, and Montana's 0% rate doesn’t apply elsewhere. The Supreme Court’s 2018 South Dakota v. Wayfair allows US states to now require that businesses with a significant presence in the state to collect sales tax. Most states set the threshold at $100,000 and/or 200 transactions, though that varies by state. If your Montana-based business has economic nexus in another state, you’re still required to register and collect sales tax there, even if you don’t have to deal with it at home. For example, a Bozeman-based company selling software, apparel, or anything else to customers in Texas , Colorado , and Washington can rack up tax obligations in all three states without ever leaving Montana. And because Montana sellers never deal with sales tax at home, they are often the last to realize they have crossed a threshold somewhere else. That’s why it’s vital to monitor your economic nexus across the US. Sphere tracks your sales against economic nexus thresholds in every US state in real time and alerts you before an obligation is triggered, so you can register on time instead of discovering the problem during an audit. Registration: What Montana Businesses Need to Register For Montana requires no general sales tax registration, because there is no sales tax to register for. There is no Montana sales tax permit. A few specific registrations still apply depending on what your business does: Resort tax registration. Businesses selling taxable goods and services inside a resort community like Big Sky or West Yellowstone register with the local municipality, not the state. Lodging tax registration. Hotels, short-term rental operators, and campgrounds register with the Montana Department of Revenue for a lodging tax account through the TransAction Portal. Income tax and withholding. Businesses with Montana employees or Montana-sourced income register for corporate income tax and employer withholding with the Montana Department of Revenue. These are income taxes, not sales taxes, but they are still real registrations with real deadlines. And if you have crossed an economic nexus threshold in another state, you register for a sales tax permit in that state. Sphere's registration agents handle those filings for you across every US jurisdiction. Ready to automate your Montana sales tax compliance? Schedule a demo with Sphere today. Book a Call Calculation: Montana Sales Tax Rates There is nothing to calculate for Montana sales tax. The rate on standard retail, SaaS, digital goods, and services is 0% everywhere in the state. No rate tables, no jurisdiction lookups, no product taxability research. The exceptions are the targeted taxes above. Businesses in resort communities calculate the local resort tax (3% to 4% depending on the community) on qualifying sales, and lodging operators calculate the combined 8% lodging tax on accommodation charges. But if you’re required to collect sales tax in other states, that gets complicated fast. The US has over 13,000 sales tax jurisdictions, and rates change constantly. Sphere calculates the correct rate automatically on every transaction in every state where you have nexus, powered by its TRAM engine , which continuously indexes tax law so the right determination is applied every time. Filing: How and When to File Montana Sales Tax Returns Montana businesses file no general sales tax returns, because no sales tax exists. There is no monthly, quarterly, or annual sales tax return, no zero-dollar filings, and no filing frequency assigned by the state. Businesses with resort tax or lodging tax accounts follow the filing schedule assigned at registration. Lodging tax returns are filed quarterly with the Montana Department of Revenue, while resort tax filing schedules are set by each local municipality. Multi-state sellers based in Montana still face filing calendars everywhere else they have nexus. Each state sets its own due dates, forms, and frequencies, and juggling twenty different deadlines by hand is where compliance usually breaks down. Sphere's filing agents prepare, validate, and submit every return on schedule across all your registered states. Remittance: How to Pay Montana Sales Tax Montana businesses remit no general sales tax to the state. There is no payment portal to set up for sales tax and no remittance deadline to track, because remitting sales tax simply is not a thing for in-state Montana sales. Businesses collecting the resort tax remit to their local municipality, and lodging operators remit the 8% lodging tax to the Montana Department of Revenue through the TransAction Portal. For out-of-state obligations, remittance runs through each state's own system, each with its own payment rules. Sphere handles remittance across all of them, including embedded remittance for foreign businesses that sell into the US without a US bank account. How Sphere Helps Montana-Based Businesses For your in-state sales, Sphere has nothing to do. Montana's 0% rate means zero registrations, zero calculations, and zero returns for sales delivered inside the state. The moment your sales cross state lines, though, the picture changes. Sphere monitors your nexus exposure across all US states, registers you where obligations arise, calculates the right rate on every transaction, files every return, and remits every payment. Exemption certificates , filing calendars, and rate changes are all handled automatically, so your team never has to become sales tax experts just because your customers live outside Montana. And in the unlikely event Montana voters ever approve a statewide sales tax, Sphere activates coverage immediately. Your compliance stack is already in place before the first return is due. ‍

title: Liberty Media Corporation Proposes Private Offering of Convertible Senior Notes
summary: ENGLEWOOD, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Liberty Media Corporation (“Liberty Media”) (Nasdaq: FWONA, FWONK) announced today that it intends to…...
body_text: Liberty Media Corporation Proposes Private Offering of Convertible Senior Notes August 10, 2026 7:14am EDT Download as PDF ENGLEWOOD, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Liberty Media Corporation (“Liberty Media”) (Nasdaq: FWONA, FWONK) announced today that it intends to offer $600 million aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes (the “Notes”) in a private offering. Liberty Media also expects to grant the initial purchasers of the Notes an option to purchase, for settlement within a period of 13 days from, and including, the date the Notes are first issued, up to an additional $90 million principal amount of Notes. The Notes will be convertible into cash, shares of Liberty Media’s Series C common stock (“FWONK”) or a combination thereof, at Liberty Media’s election. The Notes will be senior, unsecured obligations of Liberty Media, and interest will be payable semi-annually in arrears. The interest rate, initial conversion rate and other terms of the Notes will be determined at the time of pricing of the offering. Liberty Media expects to use the net proceeds of the offering to enter into capped call transactions related to its 2.25% Convertible Senior Notes due 2027 (the “2027 Notes”) and for working capital and general corporate purposes, including the repayment of the 2027 Notes. The Notes (and any shares of FWONK issuable on conversion of the Notes) will not be registered under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), or any state securities laws and, unless so registered, may not be offered or sold in the United States except pursuant to an exemption from, or in a transaction not subject to, the registration requirements of the Securities Act and applicable state securities laws. The Notes will be offered by means of an offering memorandum solely to “Qualified Institutional Buyers” pursuant to, and as that term is defined in, Rule 144A of the Securities Act. This press release does not constitute an offer to sell or the solicitation of an offer to buy any of these securities nor shall there be any sale of any of these securities in any state in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities laws of such state. About Liberty Media Corporation Liberty Media Corporation (Nasdaq: FWONA, FWONK) operates and owns interests in media, sports and entertainment businesses. The portfolio of assets includes Liberty Media’s subsidiaries Formula 1, MotoGP and other minority investments. AgentPulse expands visibility into AI agents by helping organizations discover what agents exist, who owns them, how they are being used, and where governance gaps may exist. New reporting and benchmarking capabilities make it easier to identify unmanaged agents, compare adoption trends, and investigate usage patterns, helping teams govern AI at scale with greater confidence. Adoption Analytics What’s New in AvePoint tyGraph ? New site details capabilities provide greater visibility into how AI agents interact with SharePoint content. Administrators can identify which agents are accessing specific sites, monitor activity trends over time, and review the files agents have accessed. These insights help organizations understand how AI interacts with business-critical content, support governance initiatives, and identify potential exposure risks earlier. Backup and Recovery New Backup & Recovery capabilities help organizations strengthen cyber resilience, improve visibility into protected workloads, and accelerate recovery across Microsoft 365, SaaS applications, cloud infrastructure, and business-critical services. What’s New in Cloud Backup for Microsoft 365 ? When disruptions occur, organizations need to recover critical data quickly. The new Rapid Recovery System streamlines disaster recovery with intelligent recommendations and guided recovery workflows that help teams prioritize essential business data first. By sequencing recovery around the most critical data, organizations can reduce manual triage, minimize downtime, and return users to productivity faster. Smart Recommendations help strengthen recovery readiness by automatically identifying high-priority sites based on activity, growth, size, and sensitivity. By providing greater visibility into critical business data, these insights help organizations prioritize recovery efforts and restore the information that matters most first. External sharing recovery for SharePoint helps maintain collaboration after a restore. Original external sharing settings are preserved, and previously invited external users are automatically reconnected, eliminating the need for manual reconfiguration and helping ensure business continuity. What’s new in Cloud Backup for Salesforce ? With field-level restore control , administrators can restore specific fields directly from Compare results instead of recovering an entire record. This targeted approach helps correct unwanted changes while preserving valid updates, reducing recovery risk, and simplifying data correction. What’s New in Cloud Backup for IaaS + PaaS ? Cloud Backup for IaaS + PaaS expands protection and visibility across identity and cloud infrastructure environments. Expanded Entra ID compare now supports App Registrations and Enterprise Applications, providing a more complete view of identities and configurations. The new Entra ID module centralizes identity protection and management, simplifying administration while preserving existing configurations. With IaaS & PaaS Discovery , teams can gain visibility into cloud infrastructure across Azure, AWS, and Google Cloud, identify protected and unprotected resources, and generate reports to support planning, protection, and resilience initiatives. Support for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) backup protection adds automated, snapshot-based backups for Kubernetes configurations and persistent data. Stateful applications can be restored in place or across clusters, helping reduce downtime and simplify recovery. What’s New in Cloud Backup for SaaS Applications ? Cloud Backup for SaaS Applications expands protection for business-critical platforms while giving organizations greater flexibility in how backup data is stored and managed. Organizations can now choose Amazon S3 as their default backup storage location, providing greater control over storage strategies while maintaining the same backup and recovery experience. Support for Jira Product Discovery and Trello extends backup and recovery coverage to critical product planning and collaboration data. Organizations can restore Jira Ideas, Insights, and Views, as well as Trello Workspaces, cards, comments, attachments, and custom fields, helping preserve business context and reduce disruption when data loss occurs. New ServiceNow ITSM support helps safeguard critical operational data, including incidents, requests, knowledge articles, users, groups, and configuration records. Expanded GitHub recovery coverage helps protect repositories and key configurations such as Projects, security settings, branch protection rules, permissions, Wikis, and Git Large File Storage (LFS), reducing manual effort and accelerating recovery when issues arise. What’s New in Cloud Backup for Dynamics 365 ? Smarter environment discovery and onboarding enhancements help administrators identify and connect Dynamics 365 environments more efficiently, reducing setup complexity and accelerating time to protection. What’s New in ReCenter ? Flexible data restore gives users more control over how data is recovered. Managers and end users can now restore Exchange and OneDrive content to their own account instead of the original location, making it easier to review and recover data without affecting existing content. This added flexibility helps users retrieve the information they need while reducing the risk of overwriting active data. Data Governance New data governance capabilities help organizations automate lifecycle management, strengthen accountability, and simplify the administration of Microsoft 365 resources while maintaining compliance at scale. What’s New in AvePoint Cloud Governance ? Cloud Governance expands automation, lifecycle management, and governance controls across Microsoft 365, helping organizations maintain compliance while reducing administrative effort. Automate Lifecycle Management and Ownership Accountability New capabilities help organizations govern business-critical resources throughout their lifecycle. Automated Enterprise App Renewal streamlines Entra ID application governance by combining scheduled workflows with automated MyHub outreach to validate contacts and metadata, reducing manual oversight while supporting compliance. Additional enhancements for mail contact lifecycle governance and contact election and renewal for Confide projects help organizations maintain accurate ownership records and automate renewal processes. Strengthen Governance Through Automated Controls Governance capabilities continue to expand with support for desktop flow governance for Power Automate , helping organizations manage business-critical automations with greater oversight. New standard channel provisioning also allows employees to request standard Teams channels through Dynamic Services while ensuring organizational policies and governance requirements are consistently enforced. Standardize Resource Provisioning at Scale New provisioning enhancements help organizations create more consistent Microsoft 365 environments. Dynamic metadata provisioning automatically applies metadata during the creation of Teams, Sites, and Groups, improving governance and consistency from day one. List templates further simplify SharePoint administration by enabling standardized list creation through reusable provisioning templates. Improve User Communication and Adoption With branded digest emails , organizations can customize governance notifications with their own branding, messaging, and internal guidance. This creates a more familiar user experience while helping increase engagement with governance and lifecycle management processes. What’s New in MyHub ? MyHub expands visibility and self-service governance across Microsoft 365 resources, helping administrators and workspace owners manage resources, reduce remediation effort, and simplify hybrid administration. Loop Workspace governance introduces visibility into Microsoft Loop workspaces through the MyHub Space report, allowing workspace owners and Cloud Governance contacts to view details, manage access, update settings, and take lifecycle actions from a centralized experience. To help teams focus on meaningful risks, false positive tagging allows users to quickly dismiss irrelevant findings directly from MyHub Space details and OneDrive assessments. This helps reduce noise and streamline remediation efforts. MyHub also enhances hybrid management with On-Premises group visibility and hybrid group membership support. Administrators and owners can view distribution group details, manage memberships and ownership, and update settings directly within MyHub, improving visibility across both cloud and on-premises environments. In addition, improved administrative access simplifies navigation by providing direct links to the Cloud Governance portal and MyHub Admin Portal, helping administrators access key management features more efficiently. Data Migration What’s New in AvePoint Fly ? AvePoint Fly continues to simplify complex migration scenarios with new capabilities for endpoint management, messaging modernization, and cross-platform collaboration migration. Mobile device migration helps manage the transition of iOS and Android devices across Microsoft Intune tenants by retiring corporate profiles, guiding users through re-enrollment, and automatically assigning devices to target groups and administrative units to maintain a seamless user experience. To help prepare for Microsoft's upcoming Exchange Web Services (EWS) retirement, Fly now uses Microsoft Graph API by default for Exchange Online mailbox migrations. This update supports a wide range of migration scenarios and provides administrators with the flexibility to configure alternative API modes when needed. Fly also expands migration support with Google Chat Spaces to Microsoft Teams migration , enabling organizations to move conversation history, file attachments, and member permissions directly into Microsoft Teams channels. This helps preserve collaboration context and streamline transitions from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365. Information Lifecycle Management What’s New in AvePoint Opus ? AvePoint Opus introduces new capabilities that help organizations accelerate governance framework creation, improve reporting, and strengthen records management. Now generally available, AI Recommendations helps organizations build and maintain governance frameworks more efficiently by analyzing industry, regulatory, and location-specific requirements to suggest relevant classifications, retention rules, policies, and terms. Opus data insights allows organizations to generate and export indexed Opus data directly to SharePoint Online libraries, making it easier to support Power BI reporting and analytics workflows without relying on manual exports. File Share Discovery capabilities extend Discovery and Analysis to on-premises file shares, helping organizations uncover sensitive, stale, and redundant content across legacy repositories. By bringing file share data into a unified governance experience, organizations gain greater visibility into dark data and can make more informed archiving, migration, and lifecycle management decisions. The link related records feature enables users to connect electronic records in SharePoint On-Premises with physical records stored in Opus for more consistent management and disposition. Enhanced disposal hold management capabilities provide greater oversight through hold expiration notifications, reporting enhancements, and additional controls to support audits, investigations, and legal review. Plus, smart workspace exclusion capabilities allow organizations to exclude sensitive workspaces from Discovery and Analysis scans, helping reduce noise, conserve resources, and keep reporting focused on relevant content. Access and Workflow Management What’s New in AvePoint EnPower ? AvePoint EnPower expands AI lifecycle management with new capabilities for agent ownership, renewal management, compliance reporting, and automated governance workflows. Agent timeline reports provide visibility into renewal timelines for Microsoft agents across Azure AI Foundry, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365, helping organizations track ownership and renewal activity more effectively while supporting audit and compliance requirements. Administrators can now take action directly within EnPower using manual agent renewal and manual contact election . These capabilities allow teams to trigger renewals, enrich metadata, and initiate ownership assignment workflows while maintaining accountability and audit visibility throughout the process . Automated agent governance introduces dynamic workflows for AI agents that automate ownership, compliance, and lifecycle actions across SharePoint, Microsoft 365, and Azure AI Foundry. Organizations can use activity-based, scheduled, or manually triggered workflows to enforce governance policies consistently at scale . Policies and Insights What’s new in AvePoint Policies for Microsoft 365 ? New policy enhancements help organizations enforce ownership, accountability, and governance standards across AI agents and collaboration environments. Agent ownership governance helps organizations enforce accountability for AI agents through policy-driven ownership rules. Administrators can identify agents without an active owner, review ownership gaps, and take action to ensure agents remain governed and compliant throughout their lifecycle . Channel ownership enforcement extends governance controls to private and shared Teams channels. By inheriting parent team settings or applying channel-specific restrictions, organizations can maintain consistent ownership and governance across collaboration spaces . Content-level filter conditions provide more granular policy targeting through file type-based conditions for SharePoint content. This added flexibility helps organizations apply governance controls more precisely and reduce unnecessary policy scope . What’s New in AvePoint Insights ? New Insights capabilities help organizations discover AI agents, understand potential risks, and monitor sensitive data exposure across Microsoft 365. Microsoft 365 agent insights provides a centralized view to discover, monitor Microsoft 365 agents. Enhanced dashboards, reporting, filters, and activity insights help organizations track agent risk, sensitivity, exposure, and usage while identifying high-risk, inactive, or ownerless agents . Administrators can also manage permissions, knowledge sources, and lifecycle actions from a single experience to improve governance and oversight. Granular data risk control adds more precise agent governance by defining risk based on specific sensitive data types rather than relying only on labels or sensitivity levels. This approach helps reduce false positives and improve visibility into data exposure risks , better aligning agent governance with modern Microsoft 365 data protection practices. title: How to Prioritize Tasks When Everything Is P0
summary: A practical system for ranking genuinely urgent work while keeping delayed tasks from getting lost.
body_text: How to Prioritize When Everything Is P0 Time to face a harsh truth: most prioritization advice online is useless. You can force your to-do list into an Eisenhower Matrix, color-coded Kanban board, a list of alarms on your phone, or whatever productivity framework is having its moment. But none of them answers the question that actually makes prioritization hard: What do you do when multiple things are genuinely P0? A board deck is due Friday. Your biggest customer needs an answer today. The product team cannot move until you make a decision. None of this is fake work. None of it can be ignored. And depending on who you ask, each one is correctly considered the company’s top priority. When everything is P0, the goal is not to discover which tasks matter most because, spoiler alert, they all do. The goal is to build two systems: one that forces tasks into an explicit order using consistent logic every time, and one that cleanly manages what gets delayed as a result. The first tells you what happens now. The second ensures that everything still happens later. Why Everything Feels Urgent Most productivity systems assume your work starts as a list, but executive work usually starts as a request: a board member wants revisions before Friday. Sales needs help saving a customer. Product is waiting on a decision before they can ship. On top of being never-ending, these requests almost always arrive with an “urgent” label attached to them. Sales sees the revenue at risk. Product sees the team sitting idle. The board sees the deadline. You are the person expected to see all three. That is what makes prioritization difficult: you are not just sorting one clean list of tasks by importance. You are reconciling competing commitments made to different people, often across meetings, Slack, email, and work you already delegated. And because those commitments are scattered, the loudest or most recent request tends to win by default. But—as you know very well—that is not true prioritization. Two Systems for Dealing with P0 Overwhelm System One: Create an order 1. Capture every commitment—including the ones buried in meetings and Slack Your actual workload does not live in one task manager. It is spread across meeting notes, Slack DMs, email threads, documents waiting for approval, and promises you made out loud. Before ranking anything, sweep every place where work enters your day. You cannot prioritize what you cannot see. 2. Separate what only you can do from what anyone else can do Before deciding which task comes first, remove the work that should not be competing for your time. Separate tasks that require your judgment—a strategic decision, sensitive conversation, or final call—from tasks that require your role but not your hands, like gathering information, scheduling, drafting, or routine approvals. 3. Score what remains by the cost of waiting Once the list contains only work that genuinely requires you, compare each task using the same questions: What gets worse if this waits? When does that consequence begin? What valuable work is blocked? How difficult will the decision or consequence be to reverse? This prevents the loudest, newest, or most uncomfortable request from automatically moving to the top. 4. When multiple tasks are genuinely P0, force them into a single order Several tasks can matter equally. They still cannot all happen first. When two stakeholders both have legitimate urgent requests, make the tradeoff explicit: “I can get X done by Thursday, but that moves Y to next week. Is that the right tradeoff?” The goal is not to argue that one request does not matter. It is to decide which consequence you are more willing to accept. 5. Block real time for the true top priority Once you have chosen what comes first, make your calendar reflect it. Short unblockers may need ten minutes and an immediate decision. Work that requires sustained judgment needs protected time during the hours when you think most clearly. A priority that never receives time is only a preference. System Two: Manage What Gets Delayed Choosing what comes first automatically pushes something else back. That is not a failure of prioritization. Leaving the displaced work undefined is. 6. Give every delayed or delegated task a follow-up loop Every task that does not happen now needs: An owner A next action A review date or trigger An updated expectation for whoever is waiting If the work is delegated, define what “done” means, when it is due, what could block it, and when it should return to your attention. Delegation should remove the execution from your plate—not your visibility into whether the result is still on track. Bringing It Together When everything is P0, you do not need another framework. You need visibility, an order, and a way to keep “later” from becoming “forgotten.” Get every commitment in one place. Remove the work that does not require you. Rank what remains by the cost of waiting. Then force it into a real sequence. That is prioritization: not pretending everything can happen now, but making a clear choice about what happens first while giving everything else an owner, a next step, and a reason to resurface. Bond is built around that exact loop: surfacing priorities across your tools, retaining the context behind them, and tracking commitments until they are actually complete.

title: Duke Energy announces pricing of equity units offering
summary: Duke Energy Corporation (NYSE: DUK) announced the pricing of its public offering of 35 million Equity Units.
body_text: CHARLOTTE, N.C. – Duke Energy Corporation (NYSE: DUK) announced the pricing of its public offering of 35 million Equity Units. Each Equity Unit will be issued in a stated amount of $50 ($1.75 billion aggregate stated amount) and will initially be in the form of a Corporate Unit consisting of a contract to purchase Duke Energy common stock in the future, a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in Duke Energy's 4.85% Remarketable Senior Notes due 2032 having a principal amount of $1,000 and a 1/40 undivided beneficial ownership interest in Duke Energy's 4.85% Remarketable Senior Notes due 2036 having a principal amount of $1,000. Each series of Remarketable Senior Notes is subject to remarketing, subject to certain conditions and during certain periods. The offering is expected to close on August 13, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions. Duke Energy intends to apply to list the Corporate Units on The New York Stock Exchange and expects trading to commence within 30 days of the date of initial issuance (subject to listing approval). Total distributions on the Corporate Units will be at the rate of 7.75% per year, consisting of interest payments on the Remarketable Senior Notes due 2032, interest payments on the Remarketable Senior Notes due 2036 and contract adjustment payments under the related stock purchase contracts. Under the purchase contracts, holders are required to purchase a variable number of shares of Duke Energy common stock no later than August 1, 2029. The reference price for the purchase contracts is $121.1827 per share, which is approximately equal to the closing price of Duke Energy common stock on The New York Stock Exchange on August 10, 2026. The minimum settlement rate under the purchase contracts is 0.3301 shares of Duke Energy common stock, which is approximately equal to the $50 stated amount per Equity Unit divided by the threshold appreciation price of $151.4693 per share, which represents a premium of approximately 25.00% over the reference price. The maximum settlement rate under the purchase contracts is 0.4126 shares of Duke Energy common stock, which is approximately equal to the $50 stated amount per Equity Unit divided by the reference price. Each of the settlement rates is subject to adjustment in certain circumstances. Duke Energy has granted the underwriters an option to purchase within the 13-day period beginning on, and including, the initial issuance date of the Equity Units up to 5 million additional Corporate Units (an additional $250 million aggregate stated amount), solely for the purpose of covering over-allotments. Duke Energy expects to use the net proceeds from the offering, which are expected to be approximately $1,719 million (or $1,965 million if the over-allotment option is exercised in full), after deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions but before deducting estimated offering expenses, (i) to redeem the outstanding $500 million aggregate principal amount of its 3.25% Junior Subordinated Debentures due 2082 (the “Junior Subordinated Debentures”), (ii) to repay a portion of its outstanding commercial paper and (iii) for general corporate purposes. This press release shall not constitute a notice of redemption of the Junior Subordinated Debentures or an obligation to issue a notice of redemption. Barclays, BofA Securities, Mizuho, Citigroup, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Truist Securities and Wells Fargo Securities will be book-running managers for the offering. The offering is being made under an effective shelf registration statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy the securities described herein, nor shall there be any sale of these securities in any state or jurisdiction in which such an offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful prior to registration or qualification under the securities law of any such jurisdiction. Any offers of the securities will be made exclusively by means of a prospectus supplement and accompanying prospectus. Duke Energy Duke Energy (NYSE: DUK), a Fortune 150 company headquartered in Charlotte, N.C., is one of America’s largest energy holding companies. The company’s electric utilities serve 8.7 million customers in North Carolina, South Carolina, Florida, Indiana, Ohio and Kentucky, and collectively own 55,700 megawatts of energy capacity. title: Unlocking the Power of Multiview Playback – The Future of Immersive Streaming
summary: For streaming platforms, the need to offer more dynamic, interactive, and immersive viewing experiences to set themselves apart from the competition never
body_text: This post was originally published in August 2024 and has been updated for 2026. For streaming platforms, the need to offer more dynamic, interactive, and immersive viewing experiences to set themselves apart from the competition never lets up. Sports fans crave control over how they watch their favorite games and content, and look for better options to match their viewing habits. Multiview has become one of the clearest ways platforms are meeting that demand, giving viewers a way to keep their eyes on every play or every camera angle. This Player feature gives viewers a way to get all of the live and on-demand content they want at their fingertips, especially in sports. What is Multiview? At its core, Multiview lets users view multiple video streams simultaneously on a single screen, giving them more control over how they watch. At its core, Multiview lets users view multiple video streams simultaneously on a single screen, giving them more control over how they watch. This feature can be deployed in a few ways, depending on what a platform and its viewers need most. Multiple events at once. Users can follow more than one live event on the same screen. No missed moments. Switching between games happens without leaving either one. Multiple camera angles. Viewers can follow different perspectives of the same event. Real-time angle switching. Changing the view happens instantly during live play. Ads alongside the event. Ads can run next to the main feed instead of replacing it. Uninterrupted coverage. The main action stays visible the whole time. These use cases enhance the viewing experience and empower users and platforms to curate how they engage with content. Whether sports enthusiasts want to follow multiple games or viewers look to experience events from various perspectives, Multiview brings a new level of interactivity.. The Benefits of Multiview The Multiview feature unlocks a lot of possibilities for both viewers and streaming platforms, from deeper engagement to new ways to generate revenue. Here’s where it makes the biggest difference. Enhanced engagement. Watching multiple streams keeps viewers more involved in the moment. Less churn. More engaged viewers are less likely to cancel their subscription. Premium tier potential. Multiview can be a compelling addition to higher-tier subscription plans. More ad placements. More screens on one layout means more opportunities for ad placement. Flexible ad formats. Through the Bitmovin Advertising Module (BAM), platforms can run formats like L-bar and picture-in-picture. Example of how Multiview ad playback would look with a video and a video on one screen. A social viewing experience. Groups of friends can stream different parts of a game or event together on one screen, each with their preferred angle or game. The Challenge of Multiview on Different Platforms Delivering Multiview functionality has its challenges. Higher-powered devices can run a small number of video players simultaneously without much trouble. Reliably streaming more than two to four streams at once on devices such as most TVs, which typically have only one video decoder, is a bigger hurdle. These devices can generally only display one active video stream at a time, which makes running multiple separate players unfeasible. Bitmovin addresses this with a tiled stream, encoding multiple video feeds into one, which brings several streams into a single Player instance and works even on devices limited to a single decoder. How Bitmovin is enabling customers through the Multiview Player feature Multiview is a Player feature we’ve seen a growing interest in from the streaming platforms we support, and you can see it in action with the live demo on the Multiview product page . Here’s how it works, from encoding through playback. Tiled stream creation. Bitmovin’s Live Encoder combines multiple video streams into one tiled feed. Server-side processing. The mosaic is built server-side, not on the viewer’s device. Lightweight playback. This keeps Bitmovin’s Player lightweight and playback smoother across supported devices. Example of how Multiview playback looks with 4 streams side-by-side on the Bitmovin Player. Example of how Multiview playback looks with 4 streams – one main one and 3 by its side on the Bitmovin Player. DRM-protected playback. Bitmovin’s Player is integrated with every major DRM for content security. Tile selection. Users can select any tile of interest to bring it into focus. Seamless switching. The Player switches to the high-resolution version of that stream without interrupting playback. Flexible ad formats. Platforms can run picture-in-picture, L-bar, and side-by-side ad layouts. More ad spots. Multiview increases the number of potential ad placements per event. Contextual ad matching. Ads can be matched to the event coverage. The Road Ahead While Multiview’s potential is already immense, there are also possibilities to optimize it further, such as reducing the complexity of customizing tiled streams. We’re actively exploring ways to streamline this process, possibly by reusing existing streams to avoid the need for additional encoding. Server-guided ad insertion has moved from an emerging idea to an established approach for signaling ad placement in Multiview, giving video players the information they need to show ads in the best possible locations to maximize monetization potential, beyond simple ad breaks. The future of Multiview is bright, particularly in live sports streaming, a key market for Bitmovin. As more major platforms roll out their own Multiview capabilities, it’s clear that this feature is becoming a standard expectation among viewers. Why Multiview Matters For Bitmovin and our customers, Multiview is more than just a technological advancement, it’s a strategic necessity. As the streaming landscape becomes increasingly competitive, the ability to offer unique, engaging experiences like Multiview is critical to retaining viewers and attracting new ones. For sports broadcasters and streaming services particularly, Multiview offers a way to stand out in a crowded market, giving fans the immersive, customizable experiences they crave. At Bitmovin, we’re not just responding to industry trends but shaping them. By continuing to innovate and push the boundaries of what’s possible in streaming technology, we’re helping our customers deliver the next generation of viewing experiences. Want to check it out? Multiview is available today as a standard offering on Bitmovin’s Player, with sample implementations across Web, iOS, and Android SDKs. Check out the Multiview product page for a closer look, or contact us to see how it can fit your streaming service.

title: 'Operation Safed Sagar' Contributes Over US$24 Million To India's Economy
summary: At its world premiere, Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos announced that 'Operation Safed Sagar' has contributed over US$24 million (over ₹215 crore) to the Indian economy.
body_text: As Netflix marks ten years in India, Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos announced that Operation Safed Sagar , the biggest and most ambitious Netflix India production to date, has contributed over US$24 million (over ₹215 crore) to the Indian economy. The production demonstrates The Netflix Effect — the tangible impact that Netflix shows and films have beyond the screen by generating employment, supporting local businesses, advancing creative technology and investing in talent. Speaking at the premiere, Sarandos said, “Every Netflix production is also a local production. Behind every episode are thousands of people whose creativity, skill and dedication make that story possible. The scale of this series and the production demonstrates that India today has the talent, the technical expertise and the production capabilities to create entertainment that stands confidently alongside the very best in the world.” The production engaged over 850 local businesses , more than 200 cast and crew , and 4,000 daily hires who were employed and benefited from the filming, which spanned 115 days and 11 cities, including Patiala, Gwalior, Chandigarh, Bikaner, and several others. The businesses that benefitted included local companies across construction and set-building, hospitality, transport and logistics, catering, equipment and lighting rental, VFX and post-production, and other professional services. Netflix partnered with 15 India-based VFX studios, engaging nearly 1,200 artists to produce nearly 50 minutes of breathtaking aerial sequences featured in this series. These VFX and creative-tech partnerships alone contributed more than US$5 million (₹49 crore) to India's economy, accounting for 20% of the production’s total economic contribution. “After ten years in India, we've seen The Netflix Effect come to life through every story we've had the privilege of making here. Tonight, Operation Safed Sagar is one of the most powerful expressions of that journey,” Sarandos said. The premiere was graced by the Hon'ble Minister of State for Defence Shri Sanjay Seth; Chief of Defence Staff General N.S. Raja Subramani; Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh; Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Krishna Swaminathan; Chief of the Army Staff General Dhiraj Seth; former Chief of the Air Staff Air Chief Marshal B.S. Dhanoa; Mrs. Sarita Singh, President of the Air Force Families Welfare Association; and Veer Naari Mrs. Alka Ahuja, wife of the late Squadron Leader Ajay Ahuja. They were joined by veterans, the real Golden Arrows Squadron of the Indian Air Force, and the cast and creators of Operation Safed Sagar , in a moving tribute to the courage, sacrifice, and enduring legacy of the men and women who served the nation during one of the most defining chapters in India's military history. Netflix completes ten years in India in 2026. Over the past decade, it has launched more than 200 Indian Originals , with Indian stories continuing to reach audiences worldwide while contributing to India's growing creative economy. For more stories about the impact our films and series have on economies, industries and culture, check out The Netflix Effect . title: 5 Qualities Every Successful Online English Teacher Should Have
summary: Discover five qualities that help you teach English online with confidence and create engaging online lessons for learners worldwide.
body_text: Teaching Techniques Aug 14, 2026 5 Qualities Every Successful Online English Teacher Should Have Discover five qualities that help you teach English online with confidence and create engaging online lessons for learners worldwide. What makes an online English teacher truly memorable? It's not simply how much they know about English. It's how they inspire learners to participate, create engaging online lessons, and make every learner feel comfortable enough to communicate with confidence. Every teacher brings something different to an online lesson. Some naturally motivate learners with their enthusiasm. Others explain concepts with remarkable clarity. Some create a professional learning environment that helps learners stay focused from beginning to end. While every teacher has their own teaching style, there are five qualities that consistently help teachers create meaningful online learning experiences. If you're looking to teach English online, these qualities can help you build confidence while creating enjoyable online lessons for learners around the world. 1. Passion for Teaching Passion is often the first quality learners notice. Teachers who genuinely enjoy helping others learn bring warmth, encouragement, and enthusiasm into every online lesson. Their excitement creates a positive atmosphere where learners feel motivated to participate and improve their English. Passion is reflected in the little things, from celebrating a learner's progress to patiently explaining a concept in different ways until it becomes clear. When learners see that their teacher enjoys teaching, they become more excited about learning. 2. Great Communication Skills Communication is at the heart of every successful online lesson. When you teach English online, communication goes beyond speaking fluent English. It includes giving clear instructions, asking engaging questions, listening carefully, and explaining new vocabulary in ways learners can easily understand. Strong communication also means adapting how you speak to each learner’s English level, such as using simpler words, speaking at an appropriate pace, giving clear examples, and rephrasing explanations when needed. This helps learners understand the lesson more easily and encourages them to express themselves with confidence. The clearer your communication, the more comfortable learners become using English naturally. 3. High Energy During Online Lessons In an online lesson, teachers connect with learners through a screen, which means keeping their attention requires an engaging and expressive teaching presence. High energy helps bridge that distance. A warm smile, an expressive voice, positive facial expressions, and encouraging body language can make the lesson feel more interactive and help learners stay focused and involved. Teachers should use Total Physical Response (TPR), gestures, and voice variation to reinforce meaning, explain vocabulary, and make instructions clear and easy to follow. These techniques help keep learners engaged and provide essential visual and verbal cues, especially for younger learners and beginners. By bringing positive energy to the online classroom, teachers can create a lively and supportive learning environment where learners feel comfortable participating and communicating in English. High energy isn't measured by volume. It's reflected in the way a teacher creates a warm, interactive learning environment that encourages learners to participate with confidence. 4. Professional Appearance First impressions matter, even in online lessons. Presenting yourself professionally reflects teaching excellence, builds learner confidence, and creates a welcoming learning environment from the moment the lesson begins. A professional appearance includes: Wearing a yellow shirt or plain collared shirt during classes Maintaining a neat and professional appearance while teaching Your teaching environment also contributes to your professional presence. Teach in a quiet, well-lit area with a clean and professional background, and make sure no one passes behind you or appears on camera during class. For your background, use only a solid white background or the official 51Talk tarpaulin teaching background . Curtain backgrounds and distracting or cluttered backgrounds should be avoided. A professional appearance and teaching environment help create a focused, welcoming learning experience for your learners. 5. A Reliable Teaching Setup A reliable teaching setup is the core of every successful online lesson. It provides the foundation for clear communication, uninterrupted learning, and an engaging classroom experience. Before every online lesson, ensure these core teaching essentials are in place: Stable internet connection Desktop or laptop with reliable performance Noise-canceling headset with a clear microphone High-quality webcam Proper lighting Clean, quiet, and distraction-free teaching space A reliable teaching setup is at the core of effective online teaching. It allows learners to stay focused, supports smooth lesson delivery, and reflects the professionalism and quality expected in every class. Every Great Teacher Has Unique Strengths No two online English teachers are exactly alike. Every teacher brings a unique combination of strengths—from clear communication and high energy to a professional appearance and a reliable online teaching setup. Together, these qualities create a positive learning environment where learners feel welcomed, supported, and engaged. The journey doesn't end there. With every lesson, you'll continue to strengthen these qualities, discover your authentic teaching style, and grow into an even more effective teacher who makes a lasting impact on learners. Every great teacher brings something unique to the online classroom. Your greatest strength might be your passion for teaching, the positive energy you bring to every lesson, your ability to communicate with clarity, your professional presence, or the reliable teaching setup that helps every class run smoothly. Whatever your strengths are today, they are only the beginning. Every lesson is an opportunity to learn, improve, and grow as an educator. With experience, you'll continue to build your confidence, refine your teaching style, and create meaningful learning experiences that inspire learners to succeed. Great online teaching isn't about being perfect—it's about being prepared, committed to continuous improvement, and bringing your best to every lesson. One class at a time, you'll make a positive impact on learners while growing into the teacher you aspire to be. Ready to Put These Five Qualities Into Practice? Passion, clear communication, positive energy, professionalism, and a reliable teaching setup are five qualities that can help you succeed as an online English teacher. And the best part? These are qualities you can continue to strengthen with every lesson you teach. If you're ready to bring your strengths to the online classroom, connect with learners around the world, and grow as an English teacher, 51Talk can be the place to start your teaching journey. Take the next step. Sign up with 51Talk today and start your journey toward becoming a successful online English teacher. Ready to teach online? title: PostgreSQL 19 Beta 3 is now available in Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment

body_text: Starting today, Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 19 Beta 3 is available in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment , allowing you to evaluate the pre-release of PostgreSQL 19 on Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL 19 Beta 3 adds new capabilities for query performance and autovacuum management. The new pg_stat_autovacuum_scores view helps you monitor and tune autovacuum prioritization. Parallel autovacuum can now use multiple workers to speed up maintenance on large tables. The new pg_plan_advice module lets you lock in efficient query plans to avoid unexpected slowdowns. Eager aggregation improves analytical queries by grouping data earlier, so queries process fewer rows and complete faster. Beta 3 also includes bug fixes and stability improvements from the Beta 2 testing period. Refer to the PostgreSQL community announcement for more details. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are retained for a maximum period of 60 days and are automatically deleted after the retention period. Amazon RDS database snapshots that are created in the Preview Environment can only be used to create or restore database instances within the Preview Environment. You can use the PostgreSQL dump and load functionality to import or export your databases from the Preview Environment. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are priced as per the pricing in the US East (Ohio) Region.

title: Heatwaves and Cucumber Prices: How Extreme Weather Is Driving Up Food Costs Across the UK

body_text: The effects of climate change are becoming increasingly visible in everyday life, including something as simple as buying fresh vegetables. Across the UK, shoppers are beginning to notice that cucumbers are not only becoming more expensive but also appearing noticeably more curved. While this may seem like a minor cosmetic issue, experts say it is an early sign of the growing pressure that extreme weather is placing on food production and supply chains. Following one of the driest Julys ever recorded in England and Wales, concerns are mounting over the impact of prolonged heatwaves and drought conditions on agriculture. Farmers across Europe and the UK are reporting lower crop yields, reduced quality, and higher production costs. These challenges are already influencing supermarket prices and could continue to affect consumers in the months ahead. Why Are Cucumbers Becoming More Expensive? Cucumber prices have risen significantly during the summer as unusually hot weather has disrupted growing conditions across Europe. According to figures from the Energy & Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU), the wholesale price of UK-grown cucumbers increased from around £0.99 per kilogram before the first major heatwave to approximately £2.09 per kilogram by late July. Although wholesale price increases do not always translate directly into supermarket prices, consumers often experience at least part of the increase at the checkout. Research suggests that a 10 percent increase in wholesale fruit and vegetable prices can lead to a 1 to 2 percent increase in retail prices, depending on the crop and market conditions. This means shoppers could continue paying more for fresh produce if extreme weather events become more frequent. Why Are Cucumbers Becoming Curvy? One of the more unusual effects of this year's heatwaves is the appearance of curved cucumbers. Experts explain that excessive heat makes it harder for cucumber plants to transport enough water from their roots to the developing fruit. As a result, cucumbers may grow unevenly, leading to the curved shapes now appearing more frequently in supermarkets. While curved cucumbers remain perfectly safe to eat and offer the same nutritional value as straight ones, their unusual appearance highlights how environmental stress can affect crop development. Europe's Heatwaves Are Affecting UK Food Supplies The UK relies heavily on imported fruit and vegetables throughout the year. Around 80 percent of cucumbers sold in Britain are imported, with Spain and the Netherlands among the country's largest suppliers. Both nations experienced difficult growing conditions during the recent heatwaves. In Spain, prolonged periods of extreme heat caused flowers to abort before fruit could develop properly, reducing overall harvests. Some agricultural regions also faced wildfires that further disrupted production. Meanwhile, growers in the Netherlands reported quality issues linked to elevated temperatures, including the increased occurrence of curved cucumbers. Because the UK depends on these imports, any reduction in supply can quickly influence prices for consumers. Climate Change Is Increasing Pressure on Food Production Cucumbers are only one example of how climate change is affecting agriculture. Other salad vegetables, including tomatoes, lettuce, and peppers, have also experienced production challenges due to prolonged periods of heat and drought. Lower yields mean fewer products are available for retailers, creating upward pressure on prices. Agricultural experts warn that these issues may become more common as climate extremes continue to intensify across Europe. At the same time, UK farmers are facing their own challenges. England and Wales recently experienced their driest July since records began, creating difficult conditions for growing crops and managing livestock. Many farmers have reported lower yields, increased irrigation demands, and greater concern over water availability. How Rising Food Prices Affect Consumers Food inflation does not affect every household equally. Lower income families generally spend a larger proportion of their income on groceries, meaning rising food prices place greater pressure on household budgets. Even relatively small increases in the cost of staple fruit and vegetables can make healthy eating less affordable for many people. Economists warn that if climate-related crop failures become more frequent, maintaining affordable access to nutritious food could become an increasing challenge. Will There Be Food Shortages? Despite growing concerns, experts do not currently expect widespread shortages of cucumbers or other fresh produce in the UK. Retailers often respond to supply disruptions by sourcing products from alternative countries or increasing purchases from domestic growers where possible. Advances in greenhouse production are also helping to extend the UK growing season for vegetables such as cucumbers, tomatoes, and peppers. Government officials have also stated that the UK's food system remains resilient due to a combination of domestic farming and international trade. However, while supermarket shelves are expected to remain stocked, consumers may continue to experience higher prices during periods of reduced supply. What This Means for the Future The current situation illustrates how closely food prices are linked to weather patterns around the world. As climate change contributes to more frequent heatwaves, droughts, and extreme weather events, agriculture faces increasing uncertainty. Improving water management, investing in climate-resilient farming techniques, expanding protected growing environments, and diversifying supply chains may all become essential strategies for protecting food security in the years ahead. Consumers may also notice greater seasonal variation in prices as weather conditions increasingly influence crop production. Although a curved cucumber may appear to be a small issue, it serves as a visible reminder that climate change is already affecting the food people buy every week. Final Thoughts The rise in heatwaves and cucumber prices highlights the growing connection between climate change and everyday grocery shopping. Extreme temperatures across Europe have reduced crop yields, affected produce quality, and contributed to rising wholesale prices that are beginning to reach consumers. While the UK's food supply remains stable for now, experts believe that climate resilience will become increasingly important as weather patterns continue to change. For shoppers, this may mean adapting to higher seasonal prices and occasional changes in the appearance of fresh produce, even when the food remains perfectly safe and nutritious. Source The Independent , 5 August 2026.

title: Build a Winning Business Proposal Presentation (with Examples)
summary: Learn how to build a business proposal presentation that wins the deal, from the exact slides to include to the metrics slide most decks get wrong.
body_text: August 5th, 2026 Build a Winning Business Proposal Presentation (with Examples) By Tyler Shibata · 15 min read X LinkedIn A business proposal presentation is the deck you use to pitch a solution, a plan, and a price to someone who can approve it. I've built and pitched enough of these decks to know that the difference between a yes and a stall usually comes down to a handful of slides doing their jobs well. Here's how to build a presentation that gets you a yes and leaves the polite stall behind. What is a business proposal presentation? A business proposal presentation is a slide deck that pitches your solution, plan, and pricing to whoever can approve it . That could be a prospective client, a partner, or someone deciding internally on the budget. It's the spoken, visual version of a written proposal, built to be presented live and to leave the room agreeing on a next step. Whatever you're proposing, a good presentation covers the same core parts: The problem: The situation or pain your audience is dealing with. The solution: What you're proposing to do about it. The benefits: What changes for them, in their terms. The proof: Evidence the plan works, like results, metrics, or references. The timeline: What happens, and when. The price: What it costs and what they get. The ask: The specific decision or next step you want. Structure the narrative and answer objections early The best proposal decks follow the same story: here's your problem, here's our solution, here's proof it works, here's the ask. Every slide should serve that story . Audiences care whether you understand what's broken before they care about your founding year, so open with their situation and earn the right to talk about yourself after. Naming your objections first turns weak spots into confidence: If you're the expensive option: Put the value case next to the price. If switching feels risky: Show the onboarding plan. If timing is tight: Address it directly, don’t just hope that no one asks. In my experience, a vague ask like "let us know your thoughts" invites the silence you don't want. Close on one clear decision, such as "Do we have approval to start the pilot on the 15th?" Tailor the deck to match who's in the room A client, an investor, and an internal committee all want different things, so building for the wrong one can sink a strong idea before it gets heard. Even one pitch rarely goes to a single person, since these purchases are usually cross-functional , and your deck has to answer the finance lead, the skeptic, and the day-to-day user. Here's how the deck should change depending on who's across the table: 🎯 Audience 👉 Lead with ➕ Add ✂️ Cut Client services proposal Teams with one strong anchor One clear thread the audience can follow Leans hard on the host Internal project proposal Balanced teams sharing airtime Feels natural, and nobody overshadows Abrupt handoffs without practice Vendor or procurement proposal A strong opener plus expert middle Memorable bookends and credibility Middle transitions still need rehearsal Partnership proposal Tight-knit teams, informal rooms Conversational energy Can slide into chaos and blow your timing The 10 slides your business proposal presentation needs Most winning proposal decks turn that same story into slides in a set order. I've watched decks lose momentum the moment pricing shows up before the problem feels real, so this sequence keeps the room following along: Title slide: Your company, the prospect's name, and the date. Set the frame in one line, like "A proposal to cut your onboarding time in half," so the reader knows the stakes before you get to slide two. 2. Executive summary: The whole pitch on one slide. If someone only sees this, they should still get it, since it's the one slide that has to land on its own. I've seen a strong executive summary alone buy a proposal a second meeting when nobody in the room had time to read past it. 3. The problem: Their situation, in their words. Show you understand the pain before you sell the cure, and pull language straight from what they actually told you in discovery calls. 4. Your solution: What you're proposing, described plainly. Keep the jargon out and the specifics in, since the reader wants to picture how this works for them. 5. Why you: Your differentiation and track record. A clean comparison chart against the alternatives works better here than a wall of logos, and I'd rather show three sharp differences than list ten features nobody asked about. 6. Proof and metrics: This is the numbers slide. Results, ROI, and case data, since this is often where deals get decided. I've sat in enough of these meetings to know a specific number tends to hold a room's attention longer than an adjective would, so if you only sharpen one slide, sharpen this one. 7. Timeline: What happens, and when, after they say yes. Specific dates beat vague phases like "phase one," since a calendar makes the plan feel real. 8. Pricing: The investment and what's included. Show the breakdown, so cost doesn't feel like a mystery box opened at the end. 9. Next steps: The specific ask. Name the date, the signature, or the kickoff call you need, and skip the open-ended request that invites silence. 10. Team and contact: Who they'll actually work with. Faces and names build trust that a generic "our team" slide can't. Beyond the core ten, two more slides are worth building depending on your deal: A short case study slide: Earns its spot when you have a strong result. Pick one from a client in a situation close to the prospect's if you can, since proof from a peer often lands harder than a general claim. An appendix: Worth building whenever you expect detailed questions on the numbers, since it keeps the main deck lean while the underlying math stays ready for whoever asks. 💡 Tip: Aim for 8 to 12 slides. Fewer can make you look underprepared, and more can start to read like a document projected onto a screen. How to build an effective metrics slide If I had to point to the one slide that decides most proposals, I’d say it's the metrics slide, and it's also the one I see people phone in hardest. The usual version stacks a few round, confident figures with nothing behind them, like "save 40%" or "cut reporting time in half." A sharp buyer hears that and thinks, 40% of what, measured how? Once they distrust one number, they might start doubting the rest. A convincing metrics slide shows three things: Their current cost, quantified: What the problem costs them today, in dollars, hours, or lost deals. Your projected outcome: Where your solution gets them. The gap, with its source: The difference between the two numbers is your ROI, and every figure needs a basis, whether that's their own data, a public benchmark, or your past results. Once those three numbers are solid, one clear before-and-after chart carries them further than a table of raw figures. If you're building the visual from your own data, here's how to create charts that read cleanly in a deck. Design best practices for clean business proposal presentations A proposal deck gets read in a conference room, on a laptop screen, and sometimes projected badly on a wall that washes out half your colors. Design for those conditions, since how it looks on your monitor is the least reliable preview you have. Keep these principles in mind as you build: One idea per slide: If a slide has two points, it's two slides. Headline the takeaway: "Our rollout takes 3 weeks" beats "Timeline." Keep it consistent: One font, one color system, everything aligned. A presentation maker can enforce this for you if manually checking every slide isn't practical. Make it legible from the back of the room: Big text, high contrast, and few words per slide. Use visuals with a job: A chart that proves a point earns its place. I've cut plenty of stock handshake photos from decks I've built, since they take up space without backing up a single claim. Don't lean on color alone: Some of your audience won't see red-versus-green the way you do, so label things too. 💡 Tip: Write the headline of every slide first, then read just the headlines top to bottom. If that sequence tells the whole story on its own, your structure is sound. Common mistakes that sink a business proposal presentation Small, avoidable mistakes can sink a proposal deck just as fast as a weak idea, but they're easy to fix once you know what to look for. Here are the most common ones to avoid: ❌ Mistake ✅ Fix Round, sourceless numbers Quantified, sourced ROI the buyer can check Opening with your company bio Opening with their problem A 30-slide document on a projector 8 to 12 focused slides, detail in the appendix Ending with "let us know" Ending with one specific ask Reading the slides aloud Presenting the story, slides as support One deck for every audience A version tailored to who's in the room Build a strong business proposal presentation with Julius A business proposal presentation depends on the numbers inside it, and gathering those numbers usually takes longer than building the deck itself. Julius is an AI-powered data analysis platform with a built-in AI presentation maker that lets you turn the research behind your proposal into deck-ready slides without a separate design step. Here's how Julius can support your next business proposal deck: Defensible metrics slides: Turn your cost, ROI, or savings data into a chart with a prompt, so your numbers slide shows a clear gap instead of a wall of figures. AI presentation maker : Move your analysis straight into slide form, and the chart becomes part of the deck without a separate export step. Public and financial data search: Search the web for industry benchmarks, or pull structured financials for 17,000+ public companies through the Financial Datasets integration . Connected data sources: Link tools like Postgres, Snowflake, BigQuery, or Google Ads. Any internal figures in your deck, like current costs or past project results, stay current with your own systems. More precise with every connection: Julius includes a Learning Sub Agent that picks up on your database structure as you work. Answers get faster and more precise the more you use it. Ready to build your next business proposal presentation on numbers you can defend? Try Julius for free today . Frequently asked questions How many slides should a business proposal presentation have? A business proposal presentation should have 8 to 12 slides . That's enough to walk through the problem, solution, proof, price, and ask without turning your pitch into a document. If you need more detail, move it to an appendix or the written proposal. What software is best for a business proposal presentation? PowerPoint and Google Slides give you the most control, while tools like Gamma and Beautiful.ai get you a polished deck faster. If you're stuck between two, this Gamma vs Beautiful.ai breakdown covers the tradeoffs. Should I include pricing in a business proposal presentation? Yes, most business proposal presentations should include pricing . A proposal that hides the price can make buyers nervous and stall the decision, so put pricing after you've built the value and frame it as an investment against the return you've shown. How do I turn a written proposal into a presentation? Turn a written proposal into a presentation by keeping the argument and cutting the prose . Pull out the core points, put one idea per slide, and move supporting detail into an appendix or leave the full document as a handout. How long should a business proposal presentation be? A business proposal presentation should run 10 to 20 minutes, with room left for questions . Time it in rehearsal, since decks tend to run longer out loud than they do in your head.
